name: J. R. "Russ" Wilson
bio: J. R. "Russ" Wilson was foreman of the E6 outfit south of Medora, and he hosted the Cow Boy's editor on a Black Hills trip in July 1884. His letters kept the paper posted on the E6 through winter 1884–85: in February 1885 he first wrote that losses would be small, then that the winter was unusually severe on stock, and in April 1885 he reported fat horses and a promising calf crop. In June 1885 visitors called the E6 one of the most systematic ranches they had seen, with about thirty cowboys under him. In July 1886 he discredited a story that a cowboy named Chadwick had been killed at the ranch, and in December 1886 the paper wished him and his new bride well.
